title: Mangosteen Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Mangosteen Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Mangosteen nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and phosphorus in mangostan, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Mangosteen nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your mangostan (mangosteen) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Small stunted mangosteen seedling grown without phosphorus beside a taller fully fed seedling, from phosphorus shortage
heroImage.credit: Viégas et al., American Journal of Plant Sciences 2018, CC BY 4.0, via SCIRP

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which mangosteen nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a mangosteen nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest mangosteen nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in mangosteen

No mangosteen particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The tree turns light green, the older leaves yellow evenly, veins included, and fall early. Mangosteen is slow growing anyway, but a short tree puts out even fewer and smaller flushes and takes longer to bear. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the years before bearing, and bearing trees after harvest.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in mangostan
Trees that get no fertilizer, poor sandy soils and weedy rings. Leaf nitrogen of mangosteen drops during flowering and fruiting and climbs again during leaf growth.
How to tell it apart

Young mangosteen trees need partial shade, and seedlings in full sun yellow and scorch even when well fed. Iron shortage yellows the young leaves, not the old ones. To be sure, A leaf test of mature leaves from the last flush and a soil test. Leaves that green up within weeks after a nitrogen dose confirm it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

The DA guide, based on BPI practice, gives 200 to 250 grams of complete fertilizer per tree at planting. Young trees get 300 to 500 grams of Complete 14 14 14 or 12 24 12 plus 200 to 300 grams of urea per tree per year, in two equal doses at the start and end of the rainy season, in four to six holes around the canopy edge. An Indonesian study found nitrogen raised both growth and yield.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in two splits, increase the dose as the tree grows, and add organic fertilizer, which mangosteen responds to well.
Phosphorus deficiency in mangosteen

blocks.alt: Small stunted mangosteen seedling grown without phosphorus beside a taller fully fed seedling, from phosphorus shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Viégas et al., American Journal of Plant Sciences 2018, CC BY 4.0, via SCIRP

blocks.text: No mangosteen particular leaf description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The tree grows slowly and older leaves turn dull with a purple or bronze tint, mostly underneath. In an Indonesian study, more phosphorus raised flower and fruit set and cut flower and fruit drop. So a shortage shows as poor set and heavy drop. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set, and young trees.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in mangostan
Very acid soils that hold phosphorus tightly. Leaf tests in Indonesian orchards found phosphorus at a very low status, lower than nitrogen or potassium.
How to tell it apart

Flower and fruit drop also follow drought or heavy rain at flowering. Nitrogen deficiency makes old leaves pale yellow rather than purple. To be sure, A leaf test of mature leaves and a soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Use a high phosphorus complete fertilizer such as 12 24 12, as the DA guide lists: 1.5 to 3.0 kg per bearing tree per year with potash, in two equal doses at the start and end of the rainy season. On very acid soils add lime, following the soil test, so the phosphorus stays available.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix phosphorus and compost into the planting hole, and keep a high phosphorus grade in the yearly program.
Potassium deficiency in mangosteen

blocks.alt: Mangosteen leaf with yellow blotches between the side veins toward the edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Viégas et al., American Journal of Plant Sciences 2018, CC BY 4.0, via SCIRP

blocks.text: No mangosteen particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Edges and tips of older leaves yellow, then dry brown, and the scorch moves inward. Growth slows and fewer flowers set fruit. In an Indonesian study potash raised growth and the share of flowers and fruits that set. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees during flowering and fruit growth.
Why potassium deficiency happens in mangostan
Heavy crops remove potash, and leached, acid soils under heavy rain lose it. Leaf tests in Indonesian orchards found potassium at a low to medium status.
How to tell it apart

Sun scorch on exposed young trees and dry wind also brown leaf edges, mainly on the sunny or windward side. Fertilizer burn shows soon after a heavy dose near the trunk. To be sure, A leaf test of mature leaves and a soil test for exchangeable potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

The DA guide gives bearing trees 1.5 to 3.0 kg of Complete 14 14 14 or 12 24 12 plus 200 to 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 per tree per year, in two equal doses at the start and end of the rainy season, in holes around the canopy edge. Increase it each year as the crop grows.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash every year once the tree bears, and return leaf litter and husks to the ring.
Calcium deficiency in mangosteen

The two main fruit disorders of mangosteen, translucent flesh and gamboge, are linked to calcium. With translucent flesh, some segments look glassy and water soaked, and it shows only when the fruit is opened. With gamboge, yellow gum appears in the flesh and the rind and can ooze onto the skin. The two often come together and cut the share of fruits fit to sell. You see it most at this stage: fruit growth, from about six weeks after bloom to harvest.
Why calcium deficiency happens in mangostan
Very acid soils low in nutrients. The Thai orchards in the calcium trial had soil pH of about 3.9 to 4.9.
How to tell it apart

Heavy rain during fruit growth is also tied to these disorders, so they can show even with fair calcium. Insect bites and knocks on the rind also make yellow gum ooze, but only at the wound. To be sure, cut open a sample of fruits to count glassy and gummy ones. A soil test for pH and calcium, and a leaf test.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

In a Prince of Songkla University trial, spraying Calcium chloride at 10 percent (100 grams per liter) on the fruit at 6, 7 and 8 weeks after bloom raised the share of normal fruit. Adding a little boron made it work better. This is a strong salt, so test it on a few branches first. Calcium put on the soil also lowered the disorders in earlier trials. On acid soils use Agricultural lime or Dolomite, following the soil test for the rate.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime very acid soils, keep water steady during fruit growth, and drain wet spots.
Iron deficiency in mangosteen

blocks.alt: Mangosteen seedling leaf turned yellow between a fine net of green veins, with a dead brown tip, from iron shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Viégas et al., American Journal of Plant Sciences 2018, CC BY 4.0, via SCIRP

blocks.text: Young leaves turn progressively yellow, first between the veins, while the older leaves stay green. A Brazilian study saw this on mangosteen seedlings after 12 months in a shaded nursery, with low iron and manganese in the leaves. You see it most at this stage: nursery seedlings and young trees in pots.
Why iron deficiency happens in mangostan
Mangosteen is poor at taking up iron, even from a potting mix rich in iron. High pH or overlimed mixes and soggy pots make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Manganese deficiency also yellows young leaves, but in the Brazilian trial a manganese spray did not bring the green back while an iron spray did. Nitrogen deficiency starts on the old leaves. To be sure, spray a few seedlings with iron and see if the next leaves come out green. A leaf test for iron and manganese.
What to apply for iron deficiency

Spray Ferrous sulfate mixed with a little urea on the leaves, following the label. In the Brazilian trial this greened the seedlings again. The authors also advise adding iron to the potting mix or spraying it during the nursery stage.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a slightly acid, well drained potting mix, do not overlime it, and add iron to the nursery program.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any mangosteen nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your mangostan needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Mangosteen nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my mangostan leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale, slow trees whose older leaves yellow evenly and drop, with few new flushes. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at iron deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in mangosteen?
items.a: The DA guide, based on BPI practice, gives 200 to 250 grams of complete fertilizer per tree at planting. Young trees get 300 to 500 grams of Complete 14 14 14 or 12 24 12 plus 200 to 300 grams of urea per tree per year, in two equal doses at the start and end of the rainy season, in four to six holes around the canopy edge.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in mangosteen?
items.a: Use a high phosphorus complete fertilizer such as 12 24 12, as the DA guide lists: 1.5 to 3.0 kg per bearing tree per year with potash, in two equal doses at the start and end of the rainy season. On very acid soils add lime, following the soil test, so the phosphorus stays available.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in mangosteen?
items.a: The DA guide gives bearing trees 1.5 to 3.0 kg of Complete 14 14 14 or 12 24 12 plus 200 to 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 per tree per year, in two equal doses at the start and end of the rainy season, in holes around the canopy edge. Increase it each year as the crop grows.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my mangostan lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the mangosteen nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
